stages.choice_rule: Write four different sentences of at most eight words from the roots word list plus allowed_extra_words. Exactly one sentence contains the media lemma as a whole word and matches that picture. That sentence must include oi, oy, ou, or ow in a whole word. Set answer_index to it. The other sentences must not contain the lemma. The stem is at most ten words from the same lists, may include NAME, and must not name the lemma or describe the picture. Add media with that one lemma.

roots: Exactly one sentence may match the picture. The picture lemma is a whole word in that sentence only.
The correct sentence must use oi as in coin, oy as in boy, ou as in house, or ow as in cow.
For ow and ou, use the sound in cow and house, not the long o in snow, grow, show, or yellow.
Tier 1 wrong sentences are easy and do not use oi, oy, ou, or ow.
Tier 2 has exactly one wrong sentence that uses oi, oy, ou, or ow for a different picture.
Tier 3 wrong sentences all use oi, oy, ou, or ow, and none of them match the picture.
Stay in a kid world of school, home, food, pets, play, family, and weather. No brands and no real names.
Use whole words only. Do not write a lone sound, a slash mark, or a held letter.

tier_rules.1: Five-word stems such as Which one matches the picture? The lemma is an easy noun. The correct sentence is short and obvious. Wrong sentences do not use oi, oy, ou, or ow.
tier_rules.2: About seven words in the stem. The correct sentence matches the picture with a clear diphthong word. Exactly one wrong sentence may use oi, oy, ou, or ow for a different picture.
tier_rules.3: About eight words in the stem, including NAME. Every sentence uses oi, oy, ou, or ow. Only the correct sentence matches the picture, so the other three are near misses.
